title: Waste Materials
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Children never pick broken glass, sharp tins, used syringes or medical waste; an adult handles them (SAFE).

skills.key_step: The child names waste materials that can earn money and describes how (sell to recyclers, make items, make compost), keeping away from dangerous waste.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to keep the school clean.
floor.question: Where do we put litter at school?

representations: clean waste items: bottles, tins, cartons, bottle tops
steps: Say what each can be made into or sold for.
Name waste children must never touch.
contexts: a woman weaving mats from plastic bags

board.do: Draw a plastic bottle, a tin, peels and a syringe.

board.say: Can we pick this to sell?

board.do: Wait for the child to say no, tell an adult.
Write a use beside each safe item.

misconceptions.ask: Can an empty plastic bottle earn money?
misconceptions.repair: Show items made from waste (a bottle-top toy, a tyre sandal) and a collector buying plastics.

misconceptions.ask: You see a used syringe on the dumping site. What do you do?
misconceptions.repair: Show a "never touch" list: broken glass, syringes, sharp tins, medical waste. Tell an adult.

misconceptions.ask: What is a better way to deal with plastic bottles than burning them?
misconceptions.repair: Show the black smoke from burning plastic in a picture. Say it harms the lungs and air.

misconceptions.ask: What can banana and potato peels be used for?
misconceptions.repair: Start a small compost heap at school. Show the manure after some weeks.

checks.question: Name a waste material that can earn money.
